structure: The joint law is a sex-stratified structural-equation generative model. Sex is Bernoulli with P(F)=0.54. Age is shifted Gamma(loc=18 years) with sex-specific shape and scale, giving male mean 38.1 years/SD 11.6 and female mean 43.2 years/SD 13.5. BMI is lognormal by sex with male geometric mean 21.6 kg/m^2/log SD 0.17 and female geometric mean 23.0 kg/m^2/log SD 0.19; age and log BMI are assumed independent within sex. Total cholesterol and HDL cholesterol are linear on the raw mmol/L scale in age, I(sex=F), and BMI, with bivariate normal residual errors. Residual SDs are 0.85 mmol/L for TC and 0.32 mmol/L for HDL, with residual Pearson correlation 0.12. Rare non-positive lipid draws are rejected by redrawing up to 1000 times; fallback floor is 0.05 mmol/L. Rows are generated independently and equally weighted. Because residual errors are independent of the conditioning covariates, the population OLS coefficients equal the specified structural coefficients.

parameter_provenance.unverified_assumptions: Agongo Ghanaian rural AWI-Gen age-restricted sex ratio may not match Turkana adults; source count discrepancy is preserved as unresolved.

requested_estimands.derivation: Population OLS coefficient for bmi is hdl.beta_bmi_per_kgm2 = -0.008 mmol/L per kg/m^2. Requested quantity = 5 * (-0.008) * 38.67 = -1.5468 mg/dL per 5 kg/m^2. Exogeneity of covariates makes the structural coefficient equal the population OLS coefficient.

Population OLS coefficient for bmi is tc.beta_bmi_per_kgm2 = 0.040 mmol/L per kg/m^2. Requested quantity = 5 * 0.040 * 38.67 = 7.734 mg/dL per 5 kg/m^2. Exogeneity of covariates makes the structural coefficient equal the population OLS coefficient.

The requested residual Pearson correlation equals model_spec.lipids_mmol_L.residual_correlation_tc_hdl because both OLS models condition on age, I(sex=F), and bmi and the residual errors are independent of those covariates by construction.

limitations: No Turkana 2018-2019 target outcome data are supplied; all target marginal and association parameters are explicit transfer assumptions, not validated target statistics.
Source lipid regressions are log-scale, unadjusted, partially sex-specific, and the log base is unresolved; they are not directly usable as target adjusted raw-scale OLS coefficients.
Target assay equivalence between CardioChek Plus venous-EDTA protocol and source laboratory assays is unverified. The 38.67 conversion is unit conversion only.
Target age, sex, BMI composition and lifestyle/site mixture are unspecified; the chosen composition is a synthetic approximation informed by external African adult sources.
The zero age-log BMI within-sex correlation is an assumption, not a source-supported estimate.
The bivariate normal residual distribution, shifted Gamma age distribution, and lognormal BMI distribution are parametric assumptions.
Population estimands are model-implied structural values; finite generated sample OLS estimates will differ numerically from these population values.
Source confidence intervals were not used as individual-level dispersion. Published SDs from Agongo were used only as broad dispersion prior context.
No causal interpretation is intended; requested analyses are descriptive association projections of the specified joint law.
